solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A letter said to have been used in acknowledgement

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a vowel is one kind of letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone claims a particular letter was the one used to acknowledge something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' signals that VOWAL is spoken just like VOWEL, a kind of letter; 'to have been used in' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open admission or declaration, so it is an acknowledgement.

clue.text: It is higher either side of this depressed area

definitions.text: It is higher either side of this depressed area

parts.words: It is higher either side of this depressed area
parts.note: a low-lying stretch of land with hills rising on both flanks; 'depressed' means lying low, not gloomy

explanation.surface: A gloomy region surrounded by places doing better.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is a low area of land between hills, so the ground rises on each side.

clue.text: Draw these round dividing line

indicators.note: round suggests the letters being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw some things around a line that divides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a direction for drawing, but it signals that the letters of DRAW and THESE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is the ridge separating river basins, and figuratively a turning point or dividing line.

clue.text: Illuminating cover-up

parts.note: read literally, a cover placed over something that gives light, not a revealing scandal

explanation.surface: A scandal whose concealment ends up revealing the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshade is the covering fitted over a light bulb.

clue.text: Fairly good way to rebuke

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Advice on a reasonably good method of telling someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE in the sense 'scold' is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moderate is middling or average in quality, neither poor nor excellent.

clue.text: Even soft wet earth cannot be seen at high tide

definitions.text: cannot be seen at high tide

parts.note: mud is soft wet earth
even means level, flat

explanation.surface: Level, soggy ground that disappears when the tide comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order MUD then FLAT, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflat is a stretch of coastal mud exposed only at low water and covered by the sea at high water.

clue.text: Edward brought up shy bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the piece is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward
coy is another word for shy or bashful

explanation.surface: Edward raised a timid bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ED into DE before COY is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy is a real or model bird used by hunters to lure wild fowl.

clue.text: Some more belligerently resist authority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people defy those in charge with growing aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the answer is found inside moRE BELligerently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against or defy those in power.

clue.text: Revised rate certain to produce wealth

indicators.note: revised means altered, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A reworked interest rate is bound to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges RATE together with SURE (from 'certain'); 'to produce' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a store of riches such as gold and jewels.

clue.text: Inappropriate that first person will accompany Timothy, leading journalist

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll, the first person with will
an editor, ED, is the leading journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Joining Timothy, the chief reporter, was poorly judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'accompany' only join; the apostrophe of I'LL is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-timed happens at an unsuitable moment, so it is out of place.

clue.text: Can horseflies be caught in it?

definitions.text: Can horseflies be caught in it?

parts.words: Can horseflies be caught in it?
parts.note: a fanciful thing spun to trap flies, with a hint that a cob, a sturdy horse, is part of the name

explanation.surface: A question about the best trap for biting horseflies.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a short-legged horse, and a web catches flies: the question plays on both.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobweb is a spider's web, which traps flying insects.

clue.text: Rubbish bride removed before first Saturday

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are shifted out of their places into a new order
this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: A newlywed is sent packing as garbage ahead of the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges BRIDE into DEBRI, and 'first' takes S from Saturday; 'before' places it after.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, so rubbish.

clue.text: Patriot melting alloy first

indicators.note: melting suggests the metal losing its shape and re-forming in a new order

parts.note: 1st is the short form of first, read as IST

explanation.surface: A patriotic metalworker melts the alloy before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting' rearranges ALLOY into LOYAL, then the digit 1 is read as the letter I in 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist is someone staying faithful to their country or ruler, like a patriot.

clue.text: A small hospital remains

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A little hospital is all that's left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after burning, the remains of a fire or cremation.

clue.text: Frank stirring rather hot tea

indicators.note: stirring suggests mixing the letters up as one would mix a drink

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a cup of quite hot tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it is the definition; 'stirring' rearranges RATHER HOT TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart talk is open and candid, so frank.

clue.text: Timely work quietly done on alternative melody

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
p, for piano, is the musical mark for quietly
or introduces an alternative
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A piece of music played softly to another tune arrives at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done on' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at a convenient or well-chosen moment.

clue.text: Used drill with old Penny

parts.note: a drill is a training exercise
d was the abbreviation for a penny in British money before 1971

explanation.surface: A drill was employed together with an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: D (from Latin denarius) stood for the old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, so exercised means used.

clue.text: Polished all over

definitions.meaning: refined, given a smooth final surface

explanation.definitionFit: A finished piece has had its final coat or polish, and a finished event has come to an end.

clue.text: Inn, central place of worship?

definitions.meaning: one of London's Inns of Court, where barristers belong
a temple in the middle, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Temple is one of the four Inns of Court for London barristers, and read word by word it is a temple at the centre.

clue.text: Want most of the resin

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to want is to lack

explanation.surface: A shortage of nearly all the resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims LACK to LAC; 'the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the sticky substance secreted by lac insects, used to make shellac.

clue.text: Furious fit of madness in terminus

indicators.note: in places the fit inside the word for the terminus

parts.note: a terminus is the end of a line
a rage is a fit of violent anger

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper at the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RAGE inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraged means made very angry.

clue.text: Main trouble, American hostility

indicators.note: trouble means to stir up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: The chief problem is hostility from Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges MAIN into ANIM before US is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or antagonism toward someone.

clue.text: I had backed minister, one on board

indicators.note: backed means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID
a rector is a minister of a parish

explanation.surface: I supported the priest, who sits on the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ID into DI. 'board' here is a company board, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on the governing board of a company.

clue.text: Actor's run without hitting the ball

definitions.meaning: a minor performer in a film crowd scene; the 's stands for is
in cricket a run scored without the batsman striking the ball, such as a wide or bye

explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a background performer in a film, and in cricket a run gained from byes, wides and no-balls.

clue.text: Ronald in court bringing up tips for waiters

indicators.note: in places the name inside the court abbreviation
in a down clue, bringing up means reading the letters upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: Ronald, in court, raises the matter of staff gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' turns CT into TC, and 'in' puts RON inside it. A tronc is a pool of tips shared among restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is a pooled fund of gratuities divided among restaurant staff.

clue.text: Engineers unable to withdraw

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
can't means unable

explanation.surface: Engineers find they cannot pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins; the apostrophe in CAN'T is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to take back a statement or belief formally.

clue.text: Said to obtain nothing from poor area

indicators.note: said means the clue gives the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: obtain is get, and nothing is O, together pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: A deprived district is reported to receive nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' signals that GET plus O, from 'obtain nothing', is spoken like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, often segregated, part of a city.

clue.text: Horrible having become a bit taller, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the clue gives the sound of a phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: grew some, that is grown by a little bit

explanation.surface: Something ghastly about having grown slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that 'grew some', from 'having become a bit taller', is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrifying and repellent.

clue.text: Lent moved forward

definitions.meaning: loaned money, as a bank does

explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is a loan paid up front, and troops that advanced have gone ahead.

clue.text: Senior withheld estimate that had been included

indicators.note: had been included says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning both

explanation.surface: An older official kept back a figure that was in the report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that had been included' signals the run witHELD ESTimate.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest is the oldest of a group, the most senior in age.
